subject: social-studies
title: Neighbourhood Change: One Site, Stage by Stage

questions.prompt: A student says: A neighbourhood changes all at once, because the new flats, shops and MRT station all appear in a single step. What is the best correction?

choices.text: The student is right - before-and-after photographs look completely different, so everything must have appeared at once

A neighbourhood changes stage by stage: transport links arrive first as the MRT station and bus stop open, housing blocks then rise plot by plot, and only as families move in do the shops, market and school open - the population grows at every stage, not in one jump.
The shops, market and school open first, and the flats and MRT station appear afterwards
The housing blocks rise first, and the MRT station and bus stop arrive last

questions.misconception: A neighbourhood changes all at once, because the new flats, shops and MRT station all appear in a single step.
questions.explanation: The trap claim is: A neighbourhood changes all at once, because the new flats, shops and MRT station all appear in a single step. In fact A neighbourhood changes stage by stage: transport links arrive first as the MRT station and bus stop open, housing blocks then rise plot by plot, and only as families move in do the shops, market and school open - the population grows at every stage, not in one jump.

questions.prompt: What is the first change that arrives at the site in stage 2?

choices.text: The shops, market and school open
Transport arrives first - an MRT station and a bus stop open, so the site is easy to reach
The housing blocks rise on every plot at the same time
All the families move in on the same day

questions.explanation: Scene 2 works this: transport arrives first - the MRT station and bus stop open before the housing blocks rise, and the population bar climbs one step.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, state what happens at the site between the site as found and the housing blocks rising.
questions.answer: Transport arrives first: an MRT station and a bus stop open, so the site is easy to reach before the housing blocks rise.
questions.explanation: Scene 2 runs this stage: the station and bus stop arrive while the site is still mostly houses and open ground - transport comes before homes.

questions.prompt: Explain why the population bar climbs at every stage instead of jumping once.
questions.answer: The bar climbs whenever a stage brings more people in: it starts at its lowest with a few families, climbs one step when transport arrives, climbs again as families move into the new flats, and reaches full when the replayed change is complete - 45 to 110 to 210 to 300 across the stages.
questions.explanation: The bar rises in s1 to s4 a step at a time - a few families, transport arriving, families moving in - while the all-at-once jump in s4 is the wrong turn that gets corrected.

questions.prompt: Which list gives the stages of the neighbourhood change in order?

choices.text: Low-rise houses and open ground, transport arrives first, housing blocks rise plot by plot, shops, a market and a school open as families move in
Shops, a market and a school open, housing blocks rise, transport arrives, low-rise houses and open ground
Low-rise houses and open ground, shops and a school open, transport arrives, housing blocks rise
Housing blocks rise, low-rise houses and open ground, shops and a market open, transport arrives

questions.explanation: The whole animation runs the change in that order: s1 houses and open ground, s2 transport first, s3 blocks plot by plot then shops, market and school, s4 the wrong turn corrected.
